## Paper

Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion

## World

pricing_arena

## Institution

Repeated pricing with no institution or with regulatory variants.

## Agent type

Q-learning pricing firms and higher-capability RL pricing agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Profit-normalized collusion relative to competitive and monopoly/joint-profit benchmarks.

## Learning setup

Repeated pricing game with learning agents, final-window behavior, and institution comparisons.

## Metrics

Profit-normalized collusion index, price proxy collusion index, average price, total profit, welfare, exploitability.

## Main result

Q-learning pricing algorithms systematically learn to collude by charging supracompetitive prices through finite punishment phases followed by gradual return to cooperation; collusion persists even with asymmetry, stochastic demand, and variable market structures

## What they prove

The paper provides experimental/simulation evidence that Q-learning pricing algorithms can learn supracompetitive pricing without explicit communication in the studied oligopoly settings. Treat robustness claims as model- and experiment-specific, not as universal guarantees.

## What they only simulate

Learning dynamics and pricing outcomes in simulated oligopoly pricing environments, including variants with stochastic demand and market-structure changes.

## What they do NOT test

Direct comparative evidence against human decision-makers; real-world implementation and regulatory responses

## What we need to reproduce

Report profit-normalized collusion, not only a price proxy, and interpret price-cap results using both price and profit channels.

## How our project differs

The paper anchors algorithmic collusion for Q-learning. This repo extends the question across DQN, PPO, independent-DQN, centralized critic, and institution variants.

## Implementation obligations

Profit benchmark computation; profit_collusion_index_mean in comparison tables; exploitability protocol; capability-ladder table; mechanism-specific diagnostics.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv; outputs/v1_exploitability/summary_aggregate.csv; build_combined_table.py.

## Failure modes to audit

Using only price-normalized collusion; treating capped prices as automatically non-collusive; ignoring quantity/profit channel; failing to separate exploitability from collusion.

## Project code comparison

Compare Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion to outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv. The repo now reports both price and profit collusion, making the DQN price-cap profit channel thesis-facing rather than a metric artifact.
